ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two sufficiently long parallel smooth metal rails are fixed on an inclined plane with an angle $\theta=30^{\circ}$. The resistance of the rails is negligible, and the spacing between them is L. The space where the rails are located is divided into region I and region II. The boundary between the two regions intersects the inclined plane along the line MN. In region I, there is a uniform magnetic field directed perpendicularly downward into the inclined plane, while in region II, there is a uniform magnetic field directed perpendicularly upward out of the inclined plane. The magnitudes of the magnetic induction in both regions are B. In region I, a conductor rod ab with mass $m$ and resistance $R$ is placed on the rails and is blocked by two posts. In region II, a conductor rod cd with mass $2m$ and resistance $R$ is placed on the rails and starts sliding from rest. After time t, rod ab just leaves the posts. Rods ab and cd are always perpendicular to the rails and maintain good contact with the rails at both ends. The acceleration due to gravity is g.

1. What is the magnitude of the velocity \( v_{\mathrm{t}} \) of the \( c d \) rod at time \( t \)?
2. What is the electrical energy \( E_{c d} \) generated by the \( c d \) rod in time \( t \)?
3. What is the maximum current in the $a b$ rod?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are two mutually parallel metal guide rails fixed on an inclined plane with inclination angle θ, and between the rails there are two metal rods spanning the rails and perpendicular to the rails. The dashed line MN divides the region where the guide rails are located into region I on the right side and region II on the left side. Rod ab is located in region I and is blocked by stop posts on both sides; rod cd is located in region II. In the figure, the magnetic field directions in regions I and II are opposite, both perpendicular to the inclined plane, and the magnitude of the magnetic induction intensity is B. The guide rails are placed along the direction of the inclined plane, and rod cd slides down along the inclined plane. Reasoning: Take the direction in which cd slides down along the inclined plane as the positive direction, sin30°=1/2. Before ab leaves the stop posts, it remains stationary, and only cd moves, so the magnitude of the induced electromotive force in the circuit is BLv, and the total resistance is 2R, so the current I=BLv/(2R). The magnitude of the magnetic field force on ab is BLI, and the direction of this force makes ab tend to leave the stop posts. When ab just leaves the stop posts, the magnetic field force equals the component of ab's gravity downward along the inclined plane: BLI=mg sin30°=mg/2. Substituting I=BLv_t/(2R), obtain B L · BLv_t/(2R)=mg/2, so v_t=mgR/(B^2L^2). From 0 to t, the mass of cd is 2m, the component of gravity along the inclined plane is 2mg sin30°=mg, and the magnetic field force BLI hinders the motion, so 2m dv/dτ=mg-BLI=mg-(B^2L^2/(2R))v. Let the displacement of cd during this time be x; integrating with respect to time gives 2m v_t=mg t-(B^2L^2/(2R))x, therefore x=(2R/(B^2L^2))(mg t-2m v_t). The electrical energy produced by cd equals the work done by gravity on cd minus the increase in kinetic energy of cd: E_cd=mg x-(1/2)(2m)v_t^2=mg x-mv_t^2. Substituting x and v_t=mgR/(B^2L^2), obtain E_cd=2m^2g^2Rt/(B^2L^2)-5m^3g^2R^2/(B^4L^4). After ab leaves, let the velocity of ab upward along the inclined plane be u, and the velocity of cd downward along the inclined plane be v. Since the magnetic field directions in the two regions are opposite, the circuit current I=BL(v-u)/(2R). The equations of motion are 2m dv/dτ=mg-BLI, m du/dτ=BLI-mg/2. Thus dI/dτ=(BL/(2R))(dv/dτ-du/dτ)=(BL/(2R))(g-3BLI/(2m)). The stable limit of this first-order equation is g-3BLI/(2m)=0, so the current tends to I_max=2mg/(3BL). The current at the instant of release, mg/(2BL), is less than this limit, therefore the maximum current is 2mg/(3BL).
